items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Ralph Sutton. We have a good, easy time with Ralph... He was talking about a New Year’s Eve gig that you played with Ralph Sutton.

ctx.x: How does it change your playing to work without a bass player?

Well you adjust the playing. Sometimes I just leave the hi hat off. And you play off the snare and the bass drum stays very steady. You’ve got to re-tune it where it gets a nice tone. And it all depends on that piano player see? You’ve got to have a nice, loose left © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

hand. Can’t be pounding. Teddy can play you know. There’s only one Teddy Wilson. And that’s Johnny Varro. But Johnny is very good, absolutely. And Ralph Sutton. We have a good, easy time with Ralph and we have an easy time with John Bunch, and Dave McKenna, he’s born for that, Dave McKenna is the king of that stuff. In fact he doesn’t need us. So the hell with Dave.

items.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: Jake Hanna was on drums and Rosemary Galloway was on bass. It was a trio date.

ctx.x: When was the last recording you did? It was a solo recording? I have some of your solo work.
No, the last one was this year in July I think. I did it in New York for Mat Domber. Jake Hanna was on drums and Rosemary Galloway was on bass. It was a trio date.
He’s got a nice label there. Arbors Records.
